newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake says weak market hurt Q4.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake says weak market hurt Q4.

text.p: Chesapeake Corp, reporting lower sales and earnings for the 1996 fourth quarter, said Thursday its results were affected by weak market conditions for certain products in its kraft paper business.
Start-up costs associated with several strategic growth initiatives in the packaging and tissue businesses also hurt earnings, Chesapeake said.
Price declines in the kraft segment, which saw an $89 million drop in earnings in 1996, were the "major reason for the corporation's earnings drop in 1996," it said.
The company said "significant" growth in tissue shipments helped offset the impact of these conditions and costs.

It said continuing weak market conditions in kraft products are expected to put pressure on earnings early in 1997. Some price improvement is expected later in the year, and mill efficiency continues to improve at the West Point facility, Chesapeake said.
The company also said strategic growth initiatives in the tissue and packaging businesses should increase sales and earnings in 1997.
Also during 1997, Chesapeake said, it expects to reduce its capital spending to a level close to depreciation and use any excess cash flow to reduce debt.

Capital expenditures and acquisitions for 1996 were $176 million, compared to $227 million in 1995. Chesapeake's long-term debt-to-total-capital ratio was 46 percent at the end of 1996, up from 40 percent at the end of 1995.
